dimensions.category_description: How users, artifacts, examples, parameters, or user-state signals specify intent and shape the system's next behavior.
dimensions.classification_boundary: Requires a user-facing specification or adaptive interaction; invisible sensing infrastructure is excluded.

patterns.short_summary: The system takes the interrogative turn: it poses questions — clarification prompts, structured fields, interview turns — and the user's answers, rather than a user-composed prompt, constitute the specification the system works from.
The system derives a set of discrete terms, attributes, or dimensions from the material at hand and then puts that derived set on screen as the thing the user manipulates.
Instead of describing what they want, the user supplies one or more instances of it, and the system generalizes or inverts those instances into the operative specification.

An artifact the user already possesses or has produced — a draft, a collection, a document, a physical or staged arrangement, their own prior judgments — is ingested and used as the input the generation is conditioned on.
A property of the system or of its output is bound to an ordered control the user sets to a value — a slider, a numbered keypress, a discrete set of levels, a spatial distance.
Instead of an open input box, the system attaches the same small, named menu of prepared prompts to every content unit it holds.
The user places elements on an open two-dimensional surface and the system reads their positions and relations as specification.
The user's freehand mark — a stroke, a scribble, an arrow, a drawn layout — is taken as input to generation, either alongside or in place of a written prompt.

The system holds a variable describing the user — mental state, intent, goal, emotion, skill level — and its current value selects among enumerated alternative behaviors: different strategies, presentation forms, or difficulty settings.
The user states in language what they want to be true of the artifact, and the system performs the corresponding edit or retrieval.

The system borrows the vocabulary of an already-known artifact — a spreadsheet, a paint palette, a plant, a social feed — and uses it wholesale as the surface through which the user acts, rather than devising controls specific to the underlying operation.

dimensions.category_description: When assistance appears and who triggers it: system-initiated, continuous, deferred, session-bound, or explicitly summoned.
dimensions.classification_boundary: The timing or trigger must be observable in the interaction; surface placement alone belongs to U09.

patterns.short_summary: Output is emitted without a user request immediately preceding it.

The system emits its output in step with an activity that is unfolding independently — a conversation, a performance, a learning session, a walk through an environment — so that each output appears at the moment its referent occurs.
A persistent region sits beside the surface the user is working on and shows generated content derived from that surface's current state.
The system detects something during an ongoing activity but withholds any response until the activity has ended, then presents its findings and the user's controls in a dedicated step.
Rather than an always-on stream, the system packages interaction into episodes with a defined opening and close.
A generated continuation is produced at the user's current position in the artifact being edited, and only when the user fires a control to ask for it.

dimensions.category_description: Visible rules or boundaries that restrict generation, protect artifact regions, preserve privacy, or reserve part of the task for the user.
dimensions.classification_boundary: The constraint must be expressed through the interface or directly shape an observable interaction; invisible policies are excluded.

patterns.short_summary: A structure declared in advance — a schema, slot set, section skeleton, or typed taxonomy — determines the form the model's output must take.
The user builds up a standing set of rules, principles, or preferences that is stored outside any single generation and consulted on every subsequent run.
The system runs the pipeline that would produce a terminal output but does not emit that output.
Part of the working artifact is designated off-limits and the generator is prevented from altering it, with the designation produced by the system rather than drawn by the user.

patterns.pattern_name: Low Detail Outlines with User-Filled Specificity
patterns.short_summary: The system renders its output below the fidelity it could achieve, using a sparse representation and minimal accompanying text.

dimensions.category_description: How interaction crosses sensory, physical, spatial, embodied, or representational channels.
dimensions.classification_boundary: The channel, embodiment, or rendering must be the load-bearing interface mechanism.

patterns.short_summary: The agent is given a rendered body — an animated character, a 3-D figure, an on-screen avatar, a participant tile — and the user addresses that figure rather than a text pane.
Generated content is placed in the coordinate frame of a real scene, or of captured video of one, and attached to a referent within it rather than to a panel.
A chain of generative transformations is placed inside the user's perceptual path, so that what the user perceives is the pipeline's reconstruction rather than the captured signal.
Two or more physically distinct input channels — typed text, drawn marks, speech, pointing, body pose, GUI controls — are accepted for the same operation.

At least one end of the interaction loop lives in matter rather than pixels: objects are grasped, moved, or posed to issue commands, or the system's output is delivered as physical motion, staged space, or a tangible arrangement.
The user drives the system by speaking, and the spoken utterance occupies the slot that a typed prompt or a direct-manipulation action would otherwise occupy.
One unit of system output is rendered in two or more sensory or representational channels at once — text plus speech, text plus image plus sound, or one language plus another.
A structured artifact is exposed as a traversable graph of positions that the user steps through with discrete commands, with the system's response delivered on a nonvisual channel.
The user hands a whole multi-step task to the system through a non-visual act and then stops attending to it; there is no display at any point in the loop.
Material that is not prose — extracted data, code, an algorithmic sequence, a probability, a structure — is converted into natural language and delivered in that form.

The model produces output in a representation the user cannot perceive directly — parameter streams, coordinate sequences, symbolic structures — and the system attaches a renderer that turns it into something viewable.
Rather than reusing a standard chart type, the system introduces a new graphical mark whose geometry is designed around the specific property being communicated.

dimensions.category_description: How evidence, internals, correspondence, quality, interpretations, and planned actions are represented for human judgment.
dimensions.classification_boundary: The representation must support understanding or verification, rather than merely render output into a usable medium.

patterns.short_summary: Two or more display regions show the same underlying items under different encodings, and a correspondence between them is maintained and made visible.
The pipeline from input to output passes through a named intermediate artifact that is rendered for the user to read.
The system displays its own reading of what the user supplied — the construal, the inferred intent, the context it thinks it is in — as a first-class object rather than only acting on it.
Before acting, the system displays the sequence of actions it intends to take, and that display persists as the actions are carried out.
A checkpoint is interposed between composing content and transmitting it, at which the outgoing payload is displayed to the user together with the system's assessment of it.
The same collection is presented at more than one level of granularity, from an aggregate summary down to a single item.
A large collection of items is projected into a two-dimensional layout, and that layout — not a list, not a feed — is the primary surface the user navigates.
Quantities from inside the computation — attention weights, token or answer ranks, per-head importance, the spans the model relied on — are surfaced as a view the user can read and manipulate.

Alongside an output, the system displays information about how that output came about: the derivation of a score, a confidence value, an uncertainty estimate, a quality diagnosis, or the agent's own stated reasoning.

Every unit of displayed content — a word, line, span, or segment — carries a value on some attribute, and that value is rendered by altering the appearance of the unit in place: colour, opacity, weight.
The system marks particular locations inside the user's content and attaches a deeper layer of material to each mark that is not shown until the user asks for it.
The interface puts the system's assessment next to the user's own assessment of the same thing, so the two can be read against each other.
Many underlying events or measurements are collapsed into one number on a fixed scale, and that number is the interface's headline element.

dimensions.category_description: How multiple possibilities are presented, previewed, maintained, blended, or compared before commitment.
dimensions.classification_boundary: Requires a visible choice or comparison mechanism, not backend candidate-set processing alone.

patterns.short_summary: At a single decision point the system emits more than one alternative for the same request and presents them together as a set.
Two or more instances of the same kind of artifact are displayed simultaneously in parallel regions so that their differences can be read off directly.
The interaction is organized as a tree or open graph in which alternatives coexist, rather than as a single ordered track the user advances along.
A single user request is dispatched unchanged to several distinct models at once, and their outputs are returned together.
The interface takes an input the model has already been run on, applies a controlled alteration to it, re-runs the model, and presents the altered-input output against the original one.
The user selects two or more existing items and invokes an operation whose product is a single fused result rather than either operand.

dimensions.category_description: How users inspect, modify, scope, revise, accept, program, or interrupt generated work at the artifact level.
dimensions.classification_boundary: Centers user control during or after generation, including editable intermediate generators and representations.

patterns.short_summary: The system pre-populates the working artifact with generated content that occupies its final position, and the user's task begins from that filled state.
A continuous artifact is partitioned into named units, and each unit becomes an independently addressable object.
The system opens with a concrete proposal rather than an empty field; the user reacts to it; the reaction becomes an input that yields a revised version of the same artifact.
The user designates a sub-extent of the artifact and the generative operation applies to exactly that extent.
The model's output is not the artifact the user wanted but a generator of it: code, a hierarchical program, or a parameterized template that must be executed or instantiated to yield the artifact.

A finished artifact that the system did not produce is decomposed back into an underlying structure — data table, encoding spec, component graph, layered representation — and that recovered structure becomes the object the user manipulates.
Two or more views of the same underlying object are shown at once, each of them editable, and an edit in any one propagates to the others.
Alongside the generative route, the interface keeps a route by which the user authors the same material directly: a free-text field, editable nodes, a custom operation, a user-added prompt.
Every system-produced item arrives with the same small, closed set of actions attached to it, so the user's response to any suggestion is drawn from a uniform vocabulary.
A process that would otherwise run to completion is made interruptible: the user can halt it, change its parameters while it continues, or leave it before it ends.

dimensions.category_description: How visible stages, dialogue states, histories, task decompositions, and session boundaries organize progress over time.
dimensions.classification_boundary: The process structure must be exposed to users; hidden chains of model calls are excluded.

patterns.short_summary: The sequence of conversational turns is governed by an authored control structure — a finite state machine, a protocol tree, a fixed phase sequence, a structured prompting scheme — rather than by the model's turn-by-turn discretion.
Work advances through an ordered series of stages that is fixed by the designer before the user arrives.
A goal supplied at runtime is broken into smaller sub-parts, and the parts are produced or handled serially rather than in one shot.
Prior states and actions are retained as first-class records rather than discarded when superseded.

dimensions.category_description: How AI assistance is spatially composed with artifacts, panels, host tools, chat surfaces, presentation modes, and shared workspaces.
dimensions.classification_boundary: Use for visible surface placement and integration, not sensory modality or physical-space registration.

patterns.short_summary: Task stages that were previously carried out in distinct tools, windows, or databases are placed inside one environment where they share state.
A free-form conversational channel is live at the same time as a non-conversational artifact the user is attending to, and the turns are about that artifact.
The screen is divided into a fixed number of persistent regions, each with an assigned function that does not change during use.
The same content is made available under two different presentation or interaction disciplines, and a selection determines which is in force.
The generative capability is attached to a host artifact that the system did not author — a third-party application, a web page, a chat client, an established workflow.
The interaction surface is a vertically scrolling transcript of alternating turns with a persistent composition area anchored below it.
The system's activity is rendered within the work surface itself — as cursors, marks, live strokes, or attached companions — instead of being confined to a separate conversation panel.

dimensions.category_description: How human and artificial participants are personified, assigned visible roles, coordinated, simulated, or represented to one another.
dimensions.classification_boundary: Identity or social organization must be user-facing; invisible multi-agent division of labor is excluded.

patterns.short_summary: A character specification — a name, personality, social role, or narrative voice — is attached to the generative agent and held constant across its turns.
The system generates a bounded scenario and places the user inside it as a participant rather than as an operator addressing a tool.
More than one party is present at the same system instance at the same time — two humans, a dyad, a group, or humans plus a population of agents — and the design allocates distinct roles among them.
One system presents deliberately different surfaces to different classes of participant, so what each party can see and do depends on their role.
A procedure defined over two or more roles is run by one person alone, with the model filling every role but theirs.
The object the user is authoring is instantiated as a conversational agent, and the user develops it by talking to it in character rather than by editing a representation of it.
